chunks: O men, the Apostle has now come to you, bringing the truth from your Lord; so believe for your own good; but if you deny (then remember) that all that is in the heavens and the earth belongs to God; and God is all-knowing and all-wise.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet bringing the truth from the Lord in Surah An-Nisa?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often viewed as a universal call to faith, emphasizing that belief is for the spiritual benefit of the believer, while God's sovereignty remains absolute regardless of human acceptance. It underscores the divine attribute of 'Alim' (All-Knowing) and 'Hakim' (All-Wise), reinforcing the idea that the Prophet's message is the ultimate truth from the Lord. The verse serves as a bridge between the specific call to the People of the Book and the broader humanity, highlighting the universality of Islam.
